title: Dense Numba equivalence and benchmark for the default R6D recurrence
question: Can a dense Numba implementation reproduce every frozen default R6D BP decision while materially reducing recurrence runtime?

scope.recurrence: same R6D graph, damping 0.25, 40 iterations, tolerance 1e-8

acceptance: maximum marginal difference at most 1e-12 on every record
convergence flag and iteration count identical on every record
dense posterior-LLR MWPM correction equals both Python and frozen R6N correction on every record
JIT compilation time is reported separately from warm runtime
claim_boundary: A successful benchmark validates one CPU Numba implementation of the fixed default recurrence. It does not measure GPU performance, alter the approximation, validate exact D4 posteriors, or establish asymptotic runtime scaling.
